page: Microsoft Azure E96-24s_v5 is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance belonging to the ESv5 family, featuring 24 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 12 physical cores on an x86_64 Intel Xeon 8370C processor running at 2.8 GHz. The architecture includes 105 MB of L3 cache alongside instruction set extensions such as AVX-512, AVX512_VNNI, AES-NI, and VAES. A key characteristic of this configuration is its high memory density, providing 672.0 GB of RAM, which equates to 28.0 GB per vCPU. The instance carries no bundled local storage and has no discrete GPUs.

In synthetic and operational benchmark evaluations, the instance demonstrates strong memory performance, achieving a PassMark memory score of 2894.78 and a large-block write memory bandwidth of 106.74 GB/sec, placing it in the top quartile of tested cloud hardware. CPU execution benchmarks, including stress-ng multi-core (23302.98) and PassMark CPU score (30451.25), fall into the average range. For machine learning tasks, CPU-based LLM text generation using a 135M parameter model reaches a strong 263.29 tokens per second, while prompt processing and larger model execution align with average tier results.

By constraining the core count to 24 vCPUs while providing access to 672.0 GB of memory, the instance offers qualitative cost efficiency for software licensed per vCPU or core that requires extensive system memory. The primary tradeoff is the absence of local ephemeral storage, requiring attached external block storage for persistent data needs. The hardware profile is suited for memory-intensive workloads such as large in-memory databases, enterprise resource planning systems, high-capacity Redis caches, and data analytics pipelines.
description: Microsoft Azure E96-24s_v5 is a memory-optimized virtual machine in the ESv5 series powered by a 2.8 GHz Intel Xeon 8370C processor. Built on x86_64 architecture with Hyper-V hypervisor, it features 24 dedicated vCPUs across 12 physical cores and 105 MB of L3 cache. The instance offers 672.0 GB of RAM, delivering 28.0 GB of memory per vCPU. It includes no bundled local SSD storage or discrete GPUs. Benchmark results highlight strong memory performance, including top-quartile large-block memory write bandwidth of 106.74 GB/sec and a PassMark memory score of 2894.78, alongside solid CPU execution metrics across multi-threaded tests. By decoupling high memory capacity from vCPU count, it optimizes licensing costs for memory-bound applications. The E96-24s_v5 is well suited for enterprise database management, large-scale caching services, and memory-heavy analytics workloads requiring substantial RAM per core.
